claim: GlobalFoundries renegotiated a number of its long-term agreements, including in 2025; some now have lower pricing or volume commitments than originally negotiated, and it expects a more limited number of such discussions to continue into 2026.
evidence: "We have renegotiated a number of LTAs with certain of our customers, including in 2025, as a result of which some of our LTAs now have longer commitment periods ... and some of our LTAs have lower pricing or volume commitments than originally negotiated. We expect a more limited number of these discussions to continue into 2026." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 3.D Risk Factors)
notes: Context for CLM-0177; added by fact-check fc-W0-88fb.

claim: In January 2025 an additional US$75 million of proposed CHIPS funding was added to GlobalFoundries' Direct Funding Agreement, for a new advanced packaging and test centre at its Fab 8 facility.

metric.name: Addition to CHIPS direct funding agreement
metric.population: GlobalFoundries Direct Funding Agreement with U.S. Department of Commerce

evidence: "In January 2025, an additional $75 million of proposed funding was added to the Direct Funding Agreement to support GF's plans to create a new center for advanced packaging and testing of essential chips at the Fab 8 facility." (2025 Form 20-F, Item 4)
notes: Primary-source companion to CLM-0183 (US$1.5bn, Nov 2024) and to the local-news claim about the same US$75m. Added by fc-W0-88fb.

metric.name: IFRS gross margin
metric.population: GlobalFoundries consolidated (reports under IFRS, not US GAAP)
metric.methodology: Company-reported results (earnings release furnished on 8-K); unaudited at release

evidence: "Gross margin of 24.9% and Non-IFRS gross margin(1) of 26.1%" (4Q25 earnings release, Key Full Year 2025 Financial Highlights); Summary Annual Results: "Gross margin | 24.9 %"
notes: Corrects the accounting label in CLM-0179 (GF reports under IFRS).

claim: GlobalFoundries' 2025 non-wafer revenue (NRE, masks, qualification, bump/test/packaging services, IP licensing) was US$769 million, up 17.9%, leaving US$6,022 million of wafer revenue across its four end markets.

metric.name: Non-wafer revenue
metric.population: GlobalFoundries non-wafer revenue; wafer revenue = Smart Mobile 2,678 + Comms Infra & Data Center 745 + Home & Industrial IoT 1,189 + Automotive 1,410
metric.methodology: Audited annual report (20-F revenue by end market table)

evidence: Revenue by end market table: "Smart Mobile Devices $ 2,678 ... Communications Infrastructure & Data Center 745 ... Home and Industrial IoT 1,189 ... Automotive 1,410 ... Non wafer revenue 769 | 652 | 117 | 17.9 % ... Total $ 6,791" (2025 Form 20-F, Item 5)
notes: Wafer revenue 6,022 = 6,791 - 769 (sum of the four end-market rows). Added by fc-W0-88fb.

claim: GlobalFoundries' 2025 wafer revenue divided by wafer shipments is about US$2,570 per 300mm-equivalent wafer (US$6,022m / 2,345k), a tighter estimate than total revenue per wafer (~US$2,900); it still includes some customer restructuring or underutilization payments.

metric.name: Wafer revenue per 300mm-equivalent wafer shipped
metric.population: GlobalFoundries only; wafer revenue (total less non-wafer revenue) over wafer shipments
metric.methodology: Checker division; not a disclosed ASP

evidence: Computation: (6,791 - 769) / 2,345 = 2,568. Inputs: 20-F end-market table (non-wafer revenue 769); 4Q25 release (wafer shipments 2,345 thousand). 20-F: "From time to time our wafer revenue consists of restructuring or underutilization payments from customers unable to meet their volume commitments."
notes: Refines CLM-0181; derived from the new non-wafer revenue claim and CLM-0180. Specialty/mature-node foundry, not representative of leading-edge prices.

claim: Micron states that over the past five years annual changes in DRAM average selling prices ranged from plus low-40s percent to minus high-40s percent (and for NAND from plus low-30s to minus low-50s percent).
evidence: "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low 40% to a minus high 40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low 30% to a minus low 50% range." (FY2025 Form 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors)
notes: Tightens CLM-0266's 'about -40% or worse' to the filing's 'minus high 40%'. Covers fiscal years to FY2025; the FY2026 10-K was not yet filed on 2026-10-01.

claim: Intel's 2025 gross capital expenditures were US$17.7 billion; after US$1.6 billion of capital-related government incentives and US$4.9 billion of net partner (SCIP) contributions, net capital expenditures were US$11.2 billion.

metric.name: Net capital expenditures (non-GAAP)
metric.population: Intel additions to PP&E (17,672) less capital-related government incentives (1,577) less net partner contributions (4,891)
metric.methodology: Company-reported results (earnings release furnished on 8-K); unaudited at release; non-GAAP measure defined by Intel

evidence: Twelve months 2025: "Additions to property, plant, and equipment (gross capital expenditures) (17,672)"; "Proceeds from capital-related government incentives 1,577"; "Partner contributions, net 4,891"; "Net purchase of property, plant and equipment (net capital expenditures) (11,204)" (Q4 2025 earnings release, non-GAAP reconciliation)
notes: Corrects CLM-0257, which implied the US$4.9bn covered both partners and incentives.

claim: Micron's fiscal 2026 revenue (year ended 3 September 2026) was US$133.19 billion, versus US$37.38 billion in fiscal 2025.

metric.name: Revenue
metric.methodology: Company-reported results (earnings release furnished on 8-K); unaudited at release

evidence: "Fiscal 2026 Highlights •Revenue of $133.19 billion versus $37.38 billion for the prior year"; results "for its fourth quarter and full year of fiscal 2026, which ended September 3, 2026" (8-K Ex. 99.1, 30 Sep 2026)
notes: Newer-year companion to CLM-0261. FY2026 ran to 3 Sep 2026 (by date arithmetic 53 weeks; not stated in the release). Added by fc-W0-88fb.

claim: In the year to 3 September 2026 (fiscal 2026), Micron's gross capital spending on PP&E nearly doubled to US$30.71 billion, against US$3.32 billion of government incentive proceeds.

metric.name: Expenditures for PP&E
metric.population: Micron gross capex before government incentives
metric.methodology: Company-reported results (earnings release furnished on 8-K); unaudited at release

evidence: Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (30,712) | (15,857)"; "Proceeds from government incentives | 3,316 | 2,005" (FY2026 | FY2025) (8-K Ex. 99.1)
notes: Newer-year companion to CLM-0264. Micron's non-GAAP 'investments in capital expenditures, net' was US$27.37bn.

claim: Micron's fiscal 2026 gross capital expenditures were about 23% of revenue (US$30.71bn / US$133.19bn), down from about 42% in fiscal 2025 because revenue more than tripled.
notes: Derived from the FY2026 capex and revenue claims in this batch; newer-year companion to CLM-0265.
